newsitem.title: UK: Police evict London squatters from Guinness site.
newsitem.headline: Police evict London squatters from Guinness site.

text.p: British police on Tuesday evicted a camp of "eco villagers" from derelict land in London after a five month protest aimed at highlighting environmental and housing issues.
One protester was arrested and another taken to hospital with a head injury as police moved in on the camp of about 30 people living in makeshift homes and tree houses by the River Thames.
The group called "The Land is Ours" moved onto the site, left derelict by brewing giant Guinness plc for seven years, in May and created gardens and houses.
They were protesting against plans by Guinness to build a supermarket on the site, saying the area needed low-cost housing and community amenities.
The Land is Ours is part of a small but growing group of organisations taking direct action in Britain to protest about road building, lack of housing and the increasing use of cars.
